LP u-admissibility and weights

The reference runs from A₀ to A₀ − λ. Its reflections rₖ and finite parts r̄ₖ remain fixed. The actual wall is recomputed in the current alcove at every step.

Cross is always allowed: g → gsᵢ, with v unchanged. Fold is allowed exactly when ℓ(vr̄ₖ) = ℓ(v) − 1: g stays fixed and v → vr̄ₖ. Multiplication uses (ab)(i) = a(b(i)).

Each contribution is (−1)n(J)xμ(J)[Ow], where μ(J) = −u rj₁⋯rjₛ(−λ). The exponent n(J) counts negative original reference roots at selected positions. For dominant λ and a reduced reference, all contributions are positive.

Weights are computed from the designated vertex −λ, rather than an alcove center or the image of 0 under the reference group element. This mode implements the LP K-theory rule without Ram sign filtering or q weights. It does not assert an elliptic Chevalley formula.

Lenart–Postnikov · Theorem 6.1, §18.1, Example 15.6 ↗

    Using Alcove Studio

    The yellow triangle is the fundamental alcove A₀. Its colored edges have wall types s₀ / s₁ / s₂. Click a pale green neighbor across a shared wall to add a step. Backtracking and revisiting an alcove are allowed.

    Scroll to zoom around the pointer. Hold Space and drag, or select the hand tool, to pan. Use Ctrl/⌘+Z to undo and Ctrl/⌘+Shift+Z to redo in Free Drawing mode.

    Words use right multiplication: starting at A₀, crossing a type-sᵢ wall updates w ↦ wsᵢ.

    Weights and geometric folds: Enter λ = aω₁ + bω₂ to generate a reduced reference from A₀ to A₀ − λ. A fold touches the wall and returns to the same alcove. Subsequent walls are found in the current alcove using the remaining wall types. Folded walks may have different endpoints.

    Ram mode: The reference endpoint is A₀ + λ, and the actual starting alcove can be any finite Weyl translate wA₀. Set the reference path, then choose an allowed crossing or fold at each highlighted wall, or enumerate all legal walks.

    Ram and geometric rules: All geometric folds allow either move at every step. Positive folds must stay on the positive side of the wall. Ram Theorem 3.3 requires a fold sign to equal the reference crossing sign εₖ. With w = e, no first fold is allowed, so only the reference walk remains. These rules impose no LP Bruhat-cover condition.

    LP mode: Every geometric path starts at A₀; the Schubert input u independently starts the finite Bruhat chain. The reference endpoint is A₀ − λ. Cross is always allowed. Fold is allowed exactly when ℓ(vr̄ₖ) = ℓ(v) − 1. Admissibility uses the original reference reflection, while drawing uses the current actual wall. Load Example 15.6 to see its three legal folding sets.

    LP K-theory rules: Lenart–Postnikov, Theorem 6.1, Definition 18.5, Example 15.6.

    Signed crossing and folding rules: Arun Ram, §3.1–3.2, Theorem 3.3.

    Diagram reference: affineNotes.pdf, p. 75; example paths: Example 2.19, p. 19.
